publications.title: Volatility and the cross-section of returns on FX options
publications.description: We study the cross-section of returns on FX options sorting currencies based on implied volatilities (IVs). Long straddle positions in currencies with low (high) IVs perform well (poorly). A long low IV-short high IV strategy produces large average returns after transaction costs. Total volatility matters rather than any component or transformation of volatility. The returns are distinct from those in the literature on foreign exchange returns or equity option returns and cannot be explained convincingly by standard risk factors. We argue cross-sectional differences in hedging demand combined with limits to arbitrage contribute to mispricing in FX options.

publications.title: Random Walks in Fixed Income and Foreign Exchange
publications.description:
The fixed income and foreign exchange (FX) markets have never been as challenging to operate in as they are today. The post-crash combination of reduced liquidity, higher operating costs, low interest rates, flat yield curves and increased regulation means that market makers and investors alike need to work harder to generate value and remain in full understanding of the markets.

Random Walks in Fixed Income and Foreign Exchange brings together the best of detailed and original practitioner-orientated market research on many specialist areas of the bond and FX markets. Written by the highly regarded FX and bonds research desk at Commerzbank, the book offers varied and in-depth insight into specific topics of vital important to dealers and investors, including the cross-currency basis and hedging, the yield curve, and overseas issuance conversion factors which will give investors a genuine edge in generating value. Written in accessible text, it is a must-read for all those interested in bonds and FX.

publications.title: Beyond Convexity
publications.description: Who says fixed income is boring? 100y bonds were exhibiting price swings larger than in many speculative stocks while yields were still in a relatively confined range. Duration is the main contributor and convexity an important buffer. We demonstrate how higher risk-terms become more relevant and should thus not be neglected at times when larger yield moves become more likely amid the pandemic

publications.title: Attractive and non-attractive currencies
publications.publishedAt: Journal of International Money and Finance · Sep 1, 2020
publications.description: In the foreign exchange market, time-varying transaction costs and interest rates may define the time-varying set of attractive currencies for investors. Our study shows that when the currencies are attractive, they tend to deviate from the uncovered interest rate parity and to comove with the global stochastic discount factor (SDF). Inversely, when they are non-attractive, currencies tend to conform more closely to uncovered interest parity and do not comove with the global SDF. As a consequence, both investors and policy makers may want to know the status of a currency as it conveys important information about the future return of the currency. We illustrate our point in a sample including 26 currencies over the period 1985-2017.

publications.title: An empirical method of calculating the term premium
publications.description: The term premium is important for investors, issuers and policy-makers. Negative rates emphasis the question of whether global fixed income benchmarks expose investors to rate-free risk rather than risk-free returns. Capturing the term premium allows investors to compare risk/reward across asset markets, and issuers to understand their funding cost and manage their primary market activities. For central banks, variations in the term premium can complicate the transmission of monetary policy, thus rendering the impact of actions like rate cuts and non-standard measures difficult to predict.

publications.title: Quantitative Finance
publications.description: Quantitative finance is a field that has risen to prominence over the last few decades. It encompasses the complex models and calculations that value financial contracts, particularly those which reference events in the future, and apply probabilities to these events. While adding greatly to the flexibility of the market available to corporations and investors, it has also been blamed for worsening the impact of financial crises. But what exactly does quantitative finance encompass, and where did these ideas and models originate? We show that the mathematics behind finance and behind games of chance have tracked each other closely over the centuries and that many well-known physicists and mathematicians have contributed to the field.

publications.title: FX Option Performance
publications.description: FX Options Performance is a practical handbook for successfully navigating the FX options market. Beginning with a quick overview of the market, its participants, and its products, the book then travels back in time to examine the historical payoffs to the most popular and liquidly traded option types. You'll learn which options have been consistently overvalued or undervalued, and which commonly used structures are not necessarily good value at all. The discussion also covers emerging markets and reveals truly surprising facts you won't find anywhere else — including corporate hedging strategies that reveal, in many cases, significant potential savings. Historically, some option selling strategies have been profitable, though high risk, but this book delves into the historical data to show which strategies have actually worked in the past, why they worked, and how you can mitigate risks. The companion website provides all of the detailed data in the book — over 100 tables — as easily downloadable data sets, so you can quickly start replicating these calculations and see for yourself how some simple estimates reveal historical anomalies.

publications.title: Handbook of FX Rates
publications.description: How should we evaluate the forecasting power of models? What are appropriate loss functions for major market participants? Is the exchange rate the only means of adjustment? Handbook of Exchange Rates answers these questions and many more, equipping readers with the relevant concepts and policies for working in today’s international economic climate.

Providing balanced coverage of both the practical use of models and the theory that underlies them, Interest Rate Modelling adopts an implementation orientation throughout, making it an ideal resource for both practitioners and researchers.

This is why I have always gravitated toward roles that use my relationship-building and problem-solving skills. I view my position as a consultant: understanding my clients' needs, guiding them through change, and delivering results that create long-term value. 
Alongside client work, I’ve led numerous internal change management initiatives such as automation of reporting, advising on report integration into online systems, documentation of procedures, consolidation of documentation repositories, and implementation of Docusign. Most recently, I have worked on a project that has provided invaluable lessons on how to orchestrate large-scale change in a mega-organization and how to scale those down to our smaller business unit within Citi. 

In my free time, I enjoy planning travel for others, reading, trying a new fitness class, or visiting the farmers market with my rescue dog, Ginger. 

Impactful reads: Design Your Life, Atomic Habits, The Almanack of Naval Ravikant, and The Happiness Advantage - all shaping how I approach life and work.

topSkills: Leadership Development • Management • Presentation Skills • Project Management
about:
I crave complex challenges in an environment with growth potential, creative exercise, and exciting developments. 

Here's a little about my background and how I got where I am today:

Right out of college I went to work in the non-profit world as an Income Development Representative for the American Cancer Society. At ACS I helped plan and organize community events through project management technique - keeping stats, holding status meetings and ensuring end-to-end project completion for Relay for Life events with the intention to raise funds for cancer research.

Creating change was an amazing experience and I took that mentality to Chase as a banker and immersed my brain in the financial industry throughout the financial crisis. Shortly after things started to subside, I chose to combine my work with non-profits and my career in banking and began work in JPMorgan's Commercial Bank on a portfolio of government and non-profit clients. From there I moved into project management in client onboarding where I managed the implementation of cash management products for clients in the Commercial Bank. 

After spending nearly 10 years at JPMorgan, the next phase of my career brought me to Citi to work on their Global Project Management team with Citi's most complex clients.  In this role I had the pleasure of learning a great deal about the technology sector and how they are both mom and pop shops and large multi-national corporations at the same time.   Their needs are unique and challenging and my skill set has developed immensely as a result of my interaction with them.  

I now manage a team of Program Managers in our Treasury and Trade Solutions Client Program Management Office.  Many of the organizations we support are game changers for the way the world works and it’s inspiring every single day!

experience.position: Director - Team Manager - Program Management Office, Services
Team Manager, SVP - Program Management Office, Treasury and Trade Solutions
experience.description:
In my role I am responsible for the development, growth, and empowerment of a team of Program Managers who work with global clients to deliver complex, global treasury cash management solutions.

I also drive firm objectives to enable the organization to operate with efficiency while enhancing the client experience and enabling customer success. I establish performance metrics to drive forward progress and coach my team to deliver on those goals.

As a Global Project Manager I was responsible for oversight on large, complex projects involving treasury solutions for payments and receivables.  The projects spanned multiple regions of the globe and encompassed working with regional partners to ensure a smooth client onboarding process for mergers and acquisitions, new product launches and highly visible and strategic client relationships.  My client sub-set was focused against the technology and internet sector.  I served as a central point of contact for both Citi internal teams, vendor teams and client project teams, set and maintained project governance, coordinated and oversaw the execution of project work and mobilized our vast internal organization (product teams, sales, client service, regulation, audit, legal, senior leadership) to deliver results. It was my sole responsibility to ensure project integration for both Citi, vendors and our clients.

As a senior project manager I managed the client onboarding implementation solution from inception to completion with full accountability for the end-to-end process.

As a part of this process I developed organizational process assets for managing project documentation methods and communicating deliverables and milestones.  I conducted regular project meetings to ensure adherence to the project plan and facilitated timely issue resolution if necessary. 

I also had the pleasure of participating in many projects to develop the business internally including delevoping training curriculm for our employees, developing a risk control audit process and overseeing the college intern program in our market.

As an associate in client onboarding I served as a central point of contact for our existing clients throughout the implementation of incremental business. I coordinated with internal partners to ensure delivery of products and services within an agreed upon timeframe and had full accountability for the end-to-end process of adding new products to our client's relationships.

When I transitioned to Chase's Commercial Bank I oversaw a portfolio of approximately 60 Government and Non-Profit Commercial clients with annual revenue of $50 million to $1.5 billion and maintained industry knowledge through research, internal training and networking with regional partners. I prepared and delivered sales recommendations and was the face of customer service and relationship management for each of the clients I oversaw on a daily basis.

I also participated in extra projects to establish audit and operational controls and acquired basic understanding of credit requirements for clients and the credit process of new commercial loans.

In this role I was responsible for retaining and deepening existing client relationships while performing cross-sell opportunities and product referrals to our complex sales partners. I also held Series 6 and 63 investment sales licenses.

A major feature of our Walk events is the Village In Action with interactive exhibits designed by participants from local communities. The Village in Action showcases the impact of the Foundation’s projects and provides visitors with a pathway to be engaged as global citizens.

headline: HR Analyst at Citi | UChicago & Andover Alumni

parsed.text: New York City, NY, United States

about:
As an HR Analyst at Citi, I'm eager to leverage my academic foundation in Economics and Psychology from the University of Chicago to enhance organizational effectiveness through business-oriented HR solutions.

Growing up in Bangkok, going to a boarding high school in Massachusetts, and attending college in Chicago have provided me with a global perspective and adaptability to navigate upcoming challenges. It's been quite a journey to get here, but I'm excited to explore new opportunities and future valuable experiences.

Driven by my interest in behavioral economics and organizational behavior, I prioritize blending analytical rigor with human-centric solutions to improve both processes and people. During my HR Summer Analyst internship at Citi, I helped standardize the usage of a data analytics platform, developed a business education program for HR partners, and supported organizational design projects. My experiences with Eman Equity and the Polsky Center at UChicago further strengthened my ability to integrate strategic planning, platform development, and business growth.

Beyond my professional aspirations, I am committed to lifelong learning. A few years ago, I volunteered at a vineyard in Oregon's Willamette Valley and ended up passing the WSET Level 3 Award in Wines months later. I now run the Beyond the Glass wine blog where I share the world of wine through sensations, places, and stories.

I'm always keen to connect with professionals interested in organizational effectiveness, behavioral strategies, or simply engaging conversations over a great glass of wine!

headline: VP Finance Reporting Lead Analyst.
about:
With over 13 years of experience in Banking and Corporate Services, I’ve consistently taken on high-responsibility roles with a detail-oriented mindset and a strong sense of urgency.

As a Financial Lead, I focus on cross-regional collaboration and clear communication with both management and peers to drive continuous improvement and operational efficiency.

Throughout my career, I’ve delivered ≈ $200,000 in cost savings through the development of automation templates and custom macros, streamlining core processes and enhancing performance.

experience.description: As Global Lead for key regulatory filings—including FR Y-9C, Call Report, CCAR, and 10-Q/10-K—I oversee the analysis and validation of sensitive financial data submitted to the Federal Reserve. I present findings to senior management and stakeholders ahead of submission, ensuring full compliance and transparency. My contributions have led to significant improvements in standardization, automation, and accuracy across multiple schedules, delivering measurable cost reductions and time savings.

Managed the daily production and analysis of key financial reports for the Financial & Capital Markets business, including income and balance sheets for the Money Market and Sales & Trading desks, daily liquidity, FX asset/liability balances, and deposit monitoring to support liability management and FED reporting.
Enhanced the FED Risk Pack through strategic automation, implementing quality controls that improved accuracy, reduced processing time, and delivered meaningful cost savings.

Led monthly P&L preparation, flash results, annual planning, and forecasting processes, while managing ad-hoc financial analyses and enhancing financial models to evaluate current and projected performance. Delivered comprehensive monthly and quarterly reporting packages to senior management, with emphasis on key performance indicators and variance explanations relative to Plan, Forecast, and Outlook.
Oversaw the full expense management process, providing detailed variance analyses and actionable insights to stakeholders.

Key Achievements:
Successfully delivered the full 2019 Forecasting Cycle with high recognition for accuracy and insight.

Streamlined and stabilized the retail expense and revenue share calculation process, improving transparency and creating a full Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) package.

Played a key role in establishing effective communication between Chicago and Costa Rica teams.

Served as the Leader of the VOE (Voice of the Employee) / Council initiative, fostering engagement and team alignment.

Professional Summary – QMemo Regulatory Analysis & LATAM Coordination
Led and coordinated the QMemo analysis for Banking and Corporate Mexico, benchmarking results against legacy procedures in preparation for the USRRI Platform integration. Conducted in-depth regulatory analysis aligned with US FED system requirements across LATAM, NAM, and Mexico regions.
Built and streamlined multiple communication channels to ensure timely issue resolution—leveraging IMRs, CPRs, tickets, incidents, and escalations with senior management.
Demonstrated strong product knowledge across Loans, Securities, Derivatives, Debt, Deposits, and Cash & Due balances.

Key Achievements:
Positioned Mexico as the Top Region in QMemo analysis for three consecutive quarters—the first time in three years—achieving 100% of reporting points analyzed and earning stakeholder recognition.

Successfully resolved and secured legacy issues that had remained open for over three years as part of the QMemo adoption process.

Conducted multiple training sessions within the USRRI framework, enhancing analyst performance and accelerating issue resolution across the team.

Professional Summary – Basel Reconciliation & Treasury Analysis
Served as the primary reconciliation analyst for the Basel Department, acting as the key contact for Mexico in regulatory analysis. Gained broad exposure to Global Consumer Banking products across NAM, LATAM, and Mexico.
Oversaw the full financial cycle through treasury operations, including decomposition of balances, gross and credit loss calculations, and compliance with Basel standards—specifically threshold validations required for Risk-Weighted Assets (RWA).
Also appointed as Lead for talent engagement activities, including Social Responsibility, Voice of the Employee (VOE), and Controls initiatives.

Key Achievements:
Delivered approximately $35,000 in annual savings through automation templates and macro solutions; ranked as top Bright Ideas submitter.

Named Employee of the Month (2016) in the Regulatory Reporting department for exceptional performance and cost efficiency.

Earned White Belt Certification in Citi Lean methodology.

Professional Summary – Basel Reporting & Process Optimization
Prepared accounting and financial reports for Basel, executing and consolidating retail data from multiple Citi business units into the Optima retail platform.
Led testing and validation of financial reports to identify and resolve data gaps across banking operations.
Coordinated Management Control Assessments (MCA) for audit readiness in collaboration with teams across Argentina, Costa Rica, Mexico, Brazil, and North America.

Key Achievements:
Delivered $25,000+ in annual savings through process reengineering and automation initiatives.

Recognized as Employee of the Month (July & September 2015) in the Regulatory Reporting Department for outstanding contributions to process standardization.

Professional Summary – Credit Risk Analysis & Support Operations
Performed evaluation and analysis of credit ratings for both corporate and retail clients.
Designated as Subject Matter Expert (SME) for the Net Connect platform, providing comprehensive support across helpdesk functions including data analysis, financial profile review, configuration troubleshooting, and customer satisfaction monitoring based on metrics and service productivity.

Key Achievement:
Developed a centralized technical support database, significantly improving response times and support metrics by streamlining assistance and resolution workflows.

Professional Summary – Network Administration & Security
Served as Network Administrator, responsible for the design, deployment, and maintenance of secure network infrastructure. Provided extended network support and responded effectively to urgent technical issues to ensure business continuity.

Key Achievement:
Successfully prevented a network firewall breach, securing critical data and protecting sensitive business information from a potential cyberattack.

Professional Summary – Customer Service & Technical Support (HP)
Provided front-line customer support for HP hardware and software products, delivering high-quality service with strong communication and rapport-building skills. Resolved technical issues while maintaining customer satisfaction across a broad user base.

Key Achievements:
Promoted to Subject Matter Expert (SME) in Digital Software due to product expertise and performance.

Top-ranked in customer satisfaction surveys, recognized for excellence in service quality and client engagement.

Created an interactive web dashboard using D3.js to render dynamic charts (line, bar, pie, scatter). Enabled users to upload CSV data files and explore multi-dimensional relationships via customized charts. projects.title: Predictive Modeling for House Price Estimation
projects.description:
Developed a machine learning pipeline using Linear Regression and Decision Trees to predict housing prices from real estate datasets. Performed data cleaning, normalization, outlier handling, and exploratory data analysis (EDA) using Pandas and Seaborn. Engineered features such as a number of bedrooms, square footage, and location indicators to improve model accuracy.

Trained and validated models on real-world datasets using train-test-split and cross-validation techniques. Delivered a final solution with 95 %+ accuracy onthe  validation set, emphasizing model interpretability. Proposed deployment using Flask + AWS Lambda for scalable inference APIs.

projects.title: Secure Health Records Management System
projects.description:
Developed a secure health record management system focusing on confidentiality, integrity, and controlled access to sensitive patient data.
Implemented authentication, role-based access control, and validation layers to ensure privacy and limit data exposure. Designed modules for data integrity checks, ensuring medical records are tamper-proof and trustworthy.
Built back-end logic using Python and modular architecture for scalability and maintainability. Created a web interface using Flask with support for static content and HTML templates for user-friendly access.
Ensured secure data flow between user interface and backend using structured API routes and validation logic.

projects.title: Wildfire Analysis and Management
projects.description:
Designed an end-to-end data analytics pipeline for wildfire prediction using historical datasets and weather variables. Built regression models (e.g., Linear Regression, Decision Trees) to estimate fire spread zones and intensity. Engineered a cleaned geospatial dataset and implemented feature extraction (e.g., temperature, humidity, wind speed).

Created interactive Tableau dashboards for visualization of dynamic fire risk zones across geography. Presented solution to stakeholders via a PowerPoint presentation, showcasing KPIs and predictive success metrics. Proposed integration with Google BigQuery or AWS Redshift for scalable processing of large datasets.

Explored Apache Airflow as a scheduler for automated data ingestion and daily model updates. Designed the model architecture to be deployable via Google Cloud Functions or AWS Lambda for on-demand predictions. Created an Alert system for real-time notifications based on prediction thresholds via the Twilio API or email services.

projects.title: Student-Course Management and Query System
projects.description:
Built a lightweight database-backed application to manage student enrollments and course registrations using SQLite. Designed relational database schema and implemented SQL queries for complex filtering, sorting, and data retrieval. Developed the application logic in Python with a clear separation of database and query layers.

Enabled views and data manipulation through command-line interactions, with potential for web interface. Included sample database and CRUD operations for demonstration and testing. Proposed converting the project into a RESTful API using Flask + SQLAlchemy. Deployed AWS EC2 with a front-end for broader usability.

projects.title: Face recognition attendance system using cloud computing
projects.description:
Developed a real-time face recognition attendance system using OpenCV and trained it on live webcam feeds. Implemented image preprocessing, face detection, and feature embedding to recognize and log unique individuals. Used Google Cloud Functions to integrate attendance logging into Google Sheets, enabling real-time data capture.

Designed a storage solution for student images and attendance records using structured folder hierarchies and CSV logging. Automated daily attendance summary reports using Python scripts and cron jobs. Built an interactive interface using Python (Tkinter/OpenCV windows) for real-time camera access and student feedback.

Extended functionality to support multiple face detection and misidentification warnings. Architected the pipeline to support future integration with Firebase or AWS S3 for scalable storage—applied data augmentation to improve model robustness under varied lighting and angles.

CARESOURCE REPRESENTATIVE(S) - Warren Culpepper, Rebecca Caudill

The UD Student team investigated CareSource’s IT trouble-shooting ticket process that was currently being tracked and managed manually. The team assessed the concerns that the IT department had with the goal of improving the effectiveness of manual service desk ticketing while utilizing an existing Teradata warehouse. To further process efficiency, the UD team built upon an existing BI dashboard, creating a new dashboard that not only tracks IT requests and tickets that are submitted, but also tracked the mean time to resolution for support tickets compared to the SLA (Service Level Agreement) that had been established for CareSource IT departments by its business units. In addition, the dashboard (built on MicroStrategy architecture) will generate automated reports that contain year-to-date and monthly metrics to better understand the IT department's progress.

projects.title: Mikesell's Snack Food Company: Building Brand Equity in the Minds of Millennials
projects.description:
School of Business Administration: Marketing | Capstone Project

STUDENTS: Thomas Leslie, John MacKenzie, Kathryn Estey, Shane Jabir, Benjamin Kushner
ADVISORS: Rebecca M. J. Wells, Ph.D., Tracy R. Harmon-Kizer, Ph.D.
MIKESELLS REPRESENTATIVE(S) - Luke Mapp

Mikesell's Snack Food Company was interested in identifying consumer segments that offer opportunities for long-term growth. Understanding the equity of the Mikesell's brand among consumers from various segments was critical to understanding the extent to which millenials identify with the brand and how its brand equity could be strengthened through the development of awareness, meaning, responses, and relationships.

Over the course of the 2014 calendar year, the University of Dayton team conducted primary and secondary research, completed qualitative, quantitative, and strategic analyses, and formulated recommendations for targeting viable consumer segments. The team developed a marketing research plan as well as a questionnaire and other research instruments. With assistance from faculty, data collection was administered and the students completed the data and strategic analyses. The assessment of strategic alternatives, with results and recommendations, was presented in December 2014 to the Mikesell's Snack Food Company.

headline: Architect at John Tomassi Architecture

John Tomassi is a building industry professional involved in design, construction and funding of capital development projects.  His work ranges from large footprint buildings to neighborhood and community scale planning and development projects.  

As a design firm principal from 1975 to 2007, Mr. Tomassi managed capital improvement programs for public agencies and private organizations encompassing residential, educational, institutional and commercial building types.  Since 2007, Mr. Tomassi has been engaged in real estate risk management supporting debt and equity financial services.

In service to the profession, Mr Tomassi participated in multiple civic and cultural initiatives, moderated discussions on housing and community design at AIA and ACD National conventions, and most recently partook in the Bridge 2010-2014 mentoring program for young professionals sponsored by the Chicago Chapter AIA.

Mr Tomassi currently holds positions on the Economic Development Corporation and Loan Approval Boards of Berrien County MI.  His ongoing areas of interest include whole building performance, the economics of sustainable design and the digital future of commercial real estate enterprise.

headline: Universal Banker at Citi | 131% Year to date sales | Mitigating Risk and Branch Banking (7+ years)
about:
I immigrated from Poland at a young age, and that experience shaped my work ethic, resilience, and commitment to growth. Today, I’m a Universal Banker at Citi, where I help clients navigate their financial needs with empathy, efficiency, and a personal touch. With previous experience as an Associate Banker at Chase, and customer-facing roles at a grocery store and Sunglass Hut, I’ve built a strong foundation in service, sales, and relationship-building across a range of industries. Always striving my best to maintain a minimum of 100% of my goals.

What sets me apart is my passion for delivering exceptional customer experiences. I consistently maintain customer satisfaction ratings of 90% and above by actively listening, understanding client goals, and going the extra mile to ensure their needs are met. I also thrive in team settings and enjoy building collaborative, high-performing environments where everyone feels supported and valued.

Driven, dependable, and always learning—I take pride in helping others, whether it’s a customer making an important financial decision or a teammate working toward a shared goal. I’m excited to continue growing in the financial services field and making a positive impact through service, leadership, and authentic human connection.

experience.description:
As a Universal Banker at Citi, I serve as a trusted financial partner for clients, helping them navigate a wide range of banking needs—from day-to-day transactions to personalized product recommendations that support their financial goals. My role combines customer service, sales, and relationship management, all while upholding Citi’s commitment to integrity and excellence.

95% Year-to-Date Net Promoter Score (NPS): I consistently deliver exceptional customer experiences by actively listening, providing tailored solutions, and ensuring each client feels valued and supported.

131% Year-to-Date Sales Performance: I exceed sales goals by identifying opportunities, building strong client relationships, and offering relevant financial products and services that align with customers’ needs.

In addition to sales and service, I work closely with team members to create a positive, collaborative branch environment. I’m passionate about financial education, problem-solving, and creating long-term value for both clients and the institution.

As an Associate Banker at Chase, I played a key role in delivering exceptional banking experiences while supporting branch operations and maintaining a strong compliance culture. My responsibilities extended beyond the teller line to include critical behind-the-scenes tasks that ensured the branch ran smoothly, efficiently, and in full alignment with company standards.

Key Responsibilities:

Audit & Compliance Oversight: Took ownership of internal audits, ensuring all operational procedures were followed accurately and securely, and that branch activities met regulatory requirements.
Cash Management: Handled daily cash ordering and balancing, maintaining appropriate cash levels for branch needs while minimizing risk and maximizing efficiency.
Transaction Processing: Performed a wide range of client transactions with precision and professionalism, including deposits, withdrawals, account maintenance, and check processing.
Wire Transfers: Accurately initiated and monitored domestic and international wire transfers, ensuring compliance with financial policies and client instructions.
Client Referrals: Actively identified client needs and referred them to appropriate specialists (such as bankers or financial advisors), contributing to the overall sales and service goals of the branch.
Culture Keeper: Served as the branch’s “culture keeper,” helping foster a positive, inclusive team environment and ensuring alignment with Chase’s core values. I led team engagement initiatives and contributed to a supportive, customer-focused workplace culture.
This role strengthened my attention to detail, client service skills, and operational leadership, and it gave me a deep appreciation for the balance between efficiency, compliance, and building meaningful client relationships.

As a Sales Associate at Sunglass Hut, I was responsible for delivering exceptional customer service, driving sales, and maintaining a visually compelling store environment through effective merchandising. With a strong focus on client engagement and product knowledge, I consistently exceeded performance goals, generating over $8,000 in monthly sales.

Key Responsibilities:

Delivered personalized shopping experiences by understanding customer needs and recommending the best eyewear solutions
Maintained an organized, visually appealing sales floor through strategic merchandising and product placement
Stayed up-to-date on product features and brand knowledge to enhance customer confidence and satisfaction
Contributed to a positive team environment focused on achieving daily and monthly sales targets
Supported inventory management, restocking, and store presentation to ensure a seamless shopping experience
This role strengthened my ability to connect with customers, meet and exceed sales goals, and represent premium retail brands with professionalism and enthusiasm.

I began my career at Montrose Food Mart and Deli as a cashier, where I quickly developed a strong foundation in customer service, attention to detail, and fast-paced problem solving. While my primary role was to operate the register, handle transactions, and accurately manage cash, I regularly stepped in to assist across various departments—including the bakery, deli, meat, and hot foods sections—demonstrating flexibility and a strong team-first mindset.

After just seven months, I was promoted to Customer Service, where I took on greater responsibility in supporting daily front-end operations. In this role, I:

Oversaw the cashier team, helping to manage workflows and ensure smooth operations during busy hours
Assisted with cash drawer balancing and cash preparation for armored pick-up, maintaining accuracy and security standards
Handled customer inquiries and complaints, aiming to resolve issues quickly and professionally to maintain a positive shopping experience
Acted as a point of contact between store leadership and front-end staff, helping bridge communication and support team needs
This experience taught me the importance of adaptability, leadership through service, and staying calm and resourceful in a fast-moving environment.

headline: Doctor of Built Environments I Architectural Strategy & Design Executive I Author & Columnist I Crosspollination / Design Thinking / Building Lifecycle Expert I USGBC Pro Reviewer
about:
Isilay Civan draws on 20 years of applied experience in the design and construction industry, covering most building types from office, commercial and residential buildings, to airports and healthcare facilities. Isilay’s comprehensive understanding of the entire building lifecycle from idea generation to design, to construction and occupancy, is instrumental in achieving and sustaining truly wholesome, high-performance built environments. As the Global Head of Office Design at CITI, she is responsible for the development and ongoing maintenance of future compatible workplace strategies and design guidelines, and their consistent implementation globally, as well as strategic sourcing, supplier selection and relationship management, contract negotiations, CRE/portfolio optimization analysis, design reviews, and process reengineering. 

In her past role as the firmwide Research & Strategic Innovation Specialist with HOK’s Consulting Group, Dr. Civan was responsible for cross-pollination among different sectors, running research-driven diagnostic and predictive analytics and developing evidence-based, innovative solutions for firm’s exclusive strategic accounts related to their strategic master planning, portfolio optimization, and sustainable practice initiatives. A published author of two books and over fifty technical articles and editorials, Civan earned her Bachelor’s degree in Architecture, Master’s degree in Construction Project Management and two PhDs: one in Facilities Management and the other in Real Estate Development, with a minor in Business — giving her a comprehensive understanding of the entire building spectrum.

Dr. Civan served on the IFMA Board of Directors, chaired the IFMA Research Committee and Global FM International Workshop Taskforce and was an active contributor to the IFMA Knowledge Management and EDRA CORE Committees. She sat on the Editorial Board for IFMA’s Sustainability “How-to Guides” and was one of the SMEs for IFMA’s "Sustainability Facility Professional - SFP" credential. Currently, she is an active member of USGBC and has been a GBCI Education Provider Program Reviewer and Auditor since 2009.

Specialties: workplace strategy, architectural design guide development, design thinking, evidence-based design, space planning and program development, building life-cycle, CRE/portfolio optimization, highest & best use analysis, project feasibility analysis, sustainable development, supplier relationship & performance management, strategic sourcing and contract negotiations

publications.title: The Value of Workplace Research
publications.description: In the absence of defensible evidence for the effectiveness of specific workplace strategies, designers often base planning and design decisions on experience, subjective studies or anecdotes, benchmarking and quick, limited-scope research efforts. To maximize the significant investments our clients are making on new and existing buildings, we need better workplace research tools and partners. HOK has renewed its focus on credible research-based design. In addition to committing to rigorous research efforts that inform our work, we’re advancing design research across the profession. As a collaborating partner of the Environmental Design Research Association, we have been developing a program to evaluate and recognize the quality of design research being used for all building types. We continue to work with the International Facility Management Association (IFMA), the U.S. Green Building Council, CoreNet Global, the buildingSMART alliance and other organizations to pursue better, more valid research. As a profession, we all can do better. We owe it to our clients, our credibility and the people who occupy our spaces every day to integrate the results of this true research to create the best workplace environments.

Companies are eager to understand the link between their work environments and organizational performance. The space standards and findings in this report can provide a baseline to help corporate real estate and facilities professionals identify and respond to opportunities for improvement.

publications.publishedAt: The Commercial Real Estate Network · Sep 1, 2009
publications.description:
In today’s work environment, the competitiveness of an organization is directly related with how effectively and efficiently that business manages its resources. Corporate real estate assets are termed as the fifth resource, after the traditional resources people, technology, information and capital. In addition, for many organizations, facilities-related costs are second only to the cost of labor. 

Although these two characteristics should convince organizations that judicious management of their real estate assets is a major factor, expenditures on these buildings are generally regarded as a ‘sunk’ business cost, which cannot be avoided. The prevailing view for most companies is that the level of management associated with controlling facilities-related costs is not sufficiently demanding or sophisticated enough to necessitate the skills of a specialist or the attention of the business’s senior executives. Nevertheless, companies that want to preserve their competitive edge in the market are beginning to see the importance of treating their corporate real estate as an asset and manage them accordingly at the C-Suite level.

publications.title: Ways to Prevent Office Buildings from Getting Obsolete: A Decision-Tree Approach
publications.publishedAt: VDM Verlag Dr. Mueller e.K. · Apr 18, 2008
publications.description: Office buildings are one of the major assets of companies enabling them to maintain their competitive advantage. Successful and effective facility management of corporate assets means highly efficient personnel, which translates into minimum cost and maximum profit. Preventing office buildings from getting obsolete, adaptability to change and emerging technologies protects organizations from foreseeable and excessive costs. Facilities are the infrastructure that support people in realizing their goals and require ongoing management if they are to remain aligned with their intended and primary support function. All of these facts demonstrate the indisputably important role that facilities play in corporate success. Thus, in this book, the problems that corporate buildings encounter in time and solutions for these problems are analyzed through numerous cases and systematized under certain categories. Afterward, a decision-tree that is integrated on a timeline is proposed based on the previously formed categories. This book is expected to be a useful aid for corporate managers who are aware of the unique status of their corporate real estate and are willing to take one step further to inquire about their various alternatives and find the most appropriate option to preserve the value of their assets.

publications.title: From Design to Development: An Analysis of the Go/No-Go Decision-Making Models Used in Istanbul, Turkey
publications.publishedAt: VDM Verlag Dr. Mueller e.K. · Feb 6, 2008
publications.description: Real estate development involves many complex, dynamic, and uncertain elements. In the pre-development stage, greater uncertainties result from the fact that the space being considered has not yet been created. Considering both the inherent characteristics of the real estate and the inefficiency of the market it operates, any aid in the investment decision process is believed to add to the quality of the end product. Consequently, most, if not all, of the development companies make office development decisions using some kind of a procedure in this stage. However low occupancy rates and long payback periods that is being faced, even by the most recently completed Class A office projects in Turkey, show that there are serious deficiencies in these applied procedures and that they lack the necessary components of project feasibility analysis. That's why the purpose of this book is to explore and identify the deficiencies of the decision-making models currently used by Turkish real estate development companies in the pre-development stage of office development projects and to recommend necessary additions and/or deletions for the enhancement of these company models. This work targets the primary decision-makers of the office developments, including both the national and international investors and developers.

experience.description:
"Online Tool Allows Workers to Check their Own Employment Authorization Status" (article, via U.S. Department of Homeland Security's Office of the Press Secretary's official release, dated Monday, March 21, 2011). 

On March 21, 2011, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) announced the launch of E-Verify Self Check—an innovative service that allows individuals in the United States to check their employment eligibility status before formally seeking employment.

E-Verify Self Check is the first online E-Verify program offered directly to workers and job seekers. This voluntary, free, fast and secure service was developed through a partnership between DHS and the Social Security Administration (SSA).

As of March 21, 2011, E-Verify Self Check is available to users who maintain an address and are physically located in Arizona, Idaho, Colorado, Mississippi, Virginia or the District of Columbia.

Corporate, individual et al., inclusive, applicant and user/utilizer, inclusive, of "a unique identifier assigned to suppliers to various government or defense agencies, as well as to government agencies themselves and also various organizations. CAGE codes provide a standardized method of identifying a given facility at a specific location. 
"CAGE Codes are used internationally as part of the NATO Codification System (NCS), where they are sometimes called NCAGE Codes. CAGE codes are referenced in various databases of the NCS, where they are used along with the supplier's part number to form a reference which is held on the National Stock Number (NSN) record. This reference enables users of the NCS to determine who supplies any given part.
"The information associated with the entities - name, address, phone numbers, etc. - is catalogued in the H4 and H8 Handbooks. The National Codification Bureau (NCB) of each NATO or NATO-sponsored Nation is responsible for the maintenance of the CAGE code information for entities in these respective countries. There are on the order of 1.5 Million entities in this catalog.
"Within the US, any organization wishing to be a supplier to the DoD is issued a CAGE Code by Defense Logistics Information Service (DLIS), the organization serving as the US NCB. An entity issued a CAGE code must reapply annually to renew it.
"CAGE is sometimes expanded as 'Commercial Activity/Government Entity', 'Contractor And Government Entity', or other, similar variations. According to the DLIS website, 'Commercial And Government Entity' is proper.  
"CAGE codes are all five characters in length. There is no meaning encoded in the code itself, other than the underlying NCB; it is simply a unique identifier" (all as directly quoted from the Wikipedia entry "Commercial and Government Entity code" (last modified on Friday, August 3, 2012)). Corporate, individual et al., inclusive, recipient and user/utilizer, inclusive, of “the corporate equivalent to a Social Security Number, although it is issued to anyone, including individuals, who has to pay withholding taxes on employees.
“Also known as the Federal Employer Identification Number (FEIN) or the Federal Tax Identification Number, the EIN is a unique nine-digit number assigned by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) to business entities operating in the United States for the purposes of identification. When the number is used for identification rather than employment tax reporting, it is usually referred to as a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), and when used for the purposes of reporting employment taxes, it is usually referred to as an EIN.
“Similar in purpose to the Social Security Number assigned to individuals, EINs are used by employers, sole proprietors, corporations, partnerships, non-profit organizations, trusts and estates, government agencies, certain individuals and other business entities. The IRS uses this number to identify taxpayers that are required to file various business tax returns. Individuals who are employers may choose to either obtain an EIN or use their Social Security Number for the purpose of reporting taxes withheld on behalf of their employees. Contrary to some misconceptions, credit bureaus and credit issuers can tell the difference between SSN and EIN Numbers. SSN Numbers can be validated as to origin and state / year of issuance. The credit bureaus and issuers are highly trained in fraud detection, and increasingly sophisticated algorithms and protections are used. This is why the EIN is not considered sensitive information, and is freely distributed by many businesses by way of publications and the internet" (all as directly quoted from the Wikipedia entry “Employer Identification Number” (last modified on Tuesday, November 6, 2012)).
